Suggest Bandwidth Values

Source: R/helpers.R
suggest_bandwidths.Rd

Proposes bandwidths spanning a range of spatial scales, in the units of coords.

suggest_bandwidths(
  coords,
  n_bandwidths = 5,
  range = c("medium", "local", "global"),
  distance = c("euclidean", "manhattan")
)

Arguments

coords

Coordinate matrix (N x 2)

n_bandwidths

Number of bandwidths to return

range

Character. One of "local", "medium", "global".

distance

Character. "euclidean" or "manhattan", matching what you will pass to multiScaleAC.

Value

Numeric vector of suggested bandwidths, in coordinate units, increasing. Carries a "scale_reference" attribute recording the median nearest-neighbour distance and the extent used to derive them.

Details

"local" bandwidths are derived from nearest-neighbour distances, so each cell sees a handful of neighbours. "global" bandwidths are derived from the spatial extent of the sample, so each cell sees a substantial fraction of it. "medium" spans between the two, which is usually what you want for a functional curve.

The previous version returned quantiles of the same nearest-neighbour distribution for all three settings, so "global" was not global: every option produced near-nearest-neighbour bandwidths. It also built a full N x N distance matrix, which is about 400 MB for the bundled 7122-cell example and 80 GB at N = 100000. Nearest-neighbour distances are now computed in one pass with O(N) memory.

See also

qc_neighborhoods to confirm the resulting neighbourhood sizes.

Examples

data(ccRCCExample)
coords <- as.matrix(ccRCCExample[, c("x", "y")])

# Coordinates are in millimetres, so these come back in millimetres.
h <- suggest_bandwidths(coords, n_bandwidths = 6)
round(h, 4)
#> [1] 0.0073 0.0139 0.0264 0.0501 0.0951 0.1804
#> attr(,"scale_reference")
#> median_nn_distance             extent 
#>         0.00734108         1.44298327 
attr(h, "scale_reference")
#> median_nn_distance             extent 
#>         0.00734108         1.44298327
